title: Sigil and Hollow
premise: Gideon Blackwood fled his hedge-witch master years ago, but when a smuggled grimoire names tonight's date as the night the Hollow Court beneath Thornfell collects an old debt, he discovers the debt is his own soul — sold before his birth by the mother who traded his life for her escape. To reclaim it, Gideon must descend into the Hollow Court and bargain with its dying king, whose courtiers feed on mortal memory to survive the endless winter above. Alongside Wren, a prophecy-keeper who has spent her whole life preparing a stranger for this moment, Gideon learns that every soul in the mountain was once sold too, and that freeing them means unmaking the power that keeps Thornfell's winter from devouring the world. In the end, Gideon chooses to take the king's hollow crown himself rather than let it fall to the courtiers — then shatters it, paying with his own memories of home, and walks out into the first snowfall of a true spring with Wren, carrying nothing but what he chose to keep.
about_author: Isandro Hartwell is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six winters mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. Their work blends folkloric fantasy with the quiet dread of landscapes that do not forgive.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margin
chapters.summary: Gideon, running contraband charms over the Thornfell passes, shelters in a ruined chapel where Wren shows him a century-old prophetic ledger bearing tonight's date beside his own name. He laughs it off; she does not. POV: Gideon. Beat: uneasy curiosity curdling into dread as the first snow begins out of season.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Sold
chapters.summary: Hunted by pale figures on the pass, Gideon seeks refuge with his estranged former master, Maren, who confesses the truth: his mother sold his soul to the Hollow Court before he was born, and tonight the debt comes due. POV: Gideon. Beat: betrayal and grief reframing his entire runaway life.

chapters.title: The Collectors
chapters.summary: The courtiers arrive at Maren's cottage — courteous, wrong-jointed things wearing borrowed faces. They take Maren's memories as interest and mark Gideon for collection at moonrise. Wren arrives with the ledger and a plan: there is one door into the mountain that even the court cannot close. POV: Gideon. Beat: terror tempered by resolve.

chapters.title: Wren of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Fleeing through smuggler tunnels, Wren reveals she is the last prophecy-keeper, raised to guide whoever the book named — she just never expected someone so unwilling. Their friction sparks into wary partnership. POV: Wren. Beat: loneliness meeting stubbornness, the first fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Falls
chapters.summary: At a frozen waterfall, they find the smugglers' door that predates the mountain itself, sealed with a sigil only a sold soul can open. Gideon's hand fits the mark perfectly. POV: Gideon. Beat: horror at how completely his life was never his own — and the first taste of agency in choosing to go down anyway.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: They descend through caverns where the seasons run backward: autumn, summer, spring in reverse, each stratum older and stranger. Wren teaches Gideon the ledger's cipher while he teaches her which dark corners hide teeth. POV: alternating. Beat: camaraderie forged in shared competence and rising wonder.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Debts
chapters.summary: In a cavern bazaar, mortals trade years, names, and first kisses to courtiers for warmth. Gideon recognizes a smuggler friend who no longer remembers him. POV: Gideon. Beat: the price of survival made literal; anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Dying
chapters.summary: An audience with the Hollow King, ancient and translucent, who confirms Gideon's soul sits in his treasury — but warns that his courtiers intend to devour it themselves and let the winter finish falling. He offers a bargain: bring him the crown-sigil stolen by his chancellor, and Gideon goes free. POV: Gideon. Beat: the trap inside the gift.

chapters.title: Chancellor Vesperine
chapters.summary: Vesperine, the king's chancellor, privately offers Gideon a better deal: the crown-sigil will make him king, free, powerful — all he must do is let the other souls stay sold. She shows him visions of the life he could have had. POV: Gideon. Beat: temptation that knows his name.

chapters.title: The Treasury of Souls
chapters.summary: Gideon infiltrates the treasury and finds his soul — a small burning lamp among thousands — but touching it triggers the wards. Wren pulls him out, and they learn the lamps cannot be carried out; they can only be freed from within the crown itself. POV: Wren. Beat: hope revised, not destroyed.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Hiding in the spring-stratum, Wren admits the ledger predicted a keeper would die opening the crown's final seal — and she has known since childhood. Gideon refuses to accept it. POV: Wren. Beat: guilt, tenderness, and the theme of inheritance as burden made intimate.

chapters.title: The Courtiers' Feast
chapters.summary: Summoned to the midwinter feast, Gideon watches courtiers consume a mortal's memories whole. Vesperine engineers an insult meant to force him to fight or flee; instead he publicly claims the right of challenge — an old law Wren found in the ledger. POV: Gideon. Beat: reckless courage converting fear into momentum.

chapters.title: Terms of the Challenge
chapters.summary: The challenge is set: Gideon versus Vesperine for the crown-sigil, witnessed by the dying king. Preparing, Gideon and Wren decode the final seal's requirement — a freely given memory of home, surrendered willingly. POV: alternating. Beat: strategy and dread braided together; the ticking clock of the deepening winter above.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Gift
chapters.summary: Maren, memory-stripped but alive, is brought below as leverage. Seeing her emptied, Gideon understands what victory could cost — and Maren, in a flicker of her old self, gives him the one memory she kept: his mother's face, and why she ran. POV: Gideon. Beat: compassion replacing resentment; the past forgiven if not excused.

chapters.title: The Duel of Names
chapters.summary: The duel is fought not with blades but with truths: each combatant speaks the other's true history, and lies burn the speaker. Gideon survives Vesperine's revelations about his mother because he has stopped being ashamed of them — but she wounds him with a truth about Wren's fate. POV: Gideon. Beat: painful triumph; victory that costs certainty.

chapters.title: Vesperine's Winter
chapters.summary: Defeated, Vesperine reveals her motive: she was the first sold child, and the crown is the only thing holding back the long winter — destroy it carelessly and Thornfell's world freezes. The king, she says, has been lying about what freedom costs. POV: Vesperine. Beat: the antagonist humanized; the moral ground tilting.

chapters.title: The King's Confession
chapters.summary: Confronting the Hollow King, Gideon learns the truth: the king created the debt-system to feed the crown, and the 'long winter' is the crown's own hunger projected outward. Ending it will hurt — but it will end. POV: Gideon. Beat: clarity; the corrupting architecture of power laid bare.

chapters.title: The Crown-Sigil
chapters.summary: Gideon takes the crown-sigil from the fallen king's brow and feels its hunger immediately — the seductive ease of command, the courtiers kneeling unbidden. He nearly puts it on. Wren's voice calls him back. POV: Gideon. Beat: the climax of temptation; power offered and refused at the brink.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: At the crown's heart, Wren gives her promised memory willingly and opens the final seal; Gideon shatters the sigil with the one thing the court cannot buy — his choice, made freely. The lamps ignite, souls streaming upward through the mountain like reversed snowfall. POV: alternating. Beat: sacrifice, release, and awe.

chapters.title: What He Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: Gideon wakes on the mountainside lighter by whole years of memory — his mother's face gone, his master's cottage dim — but himself in a way he never was. Freed souls scatter homeward; Vesperine, mortal now, walks into the dawn without hatred. POV: Gideon. Beat: grief and peace entwined; the price paid and accepted.

chapters.title: First Snow of Spring
chapters.summary: Thornfell thaws out of season. Wren, alive though her ledger is blank at last, and Gideon bury the book beneath the falls and argue pleasantly about which road to take down the mountain. POV: Wren. Beat: warmth, humor, and the quiet beginning of something chosen rather than fated.

chapters.title: Sigil and Hollow
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Gideon runs honest roads again, and travelers speak of a scarred man who buys back debts for a living. On his palm, faint as frost, the old sigil remains — not a brand now, but a reminder. POV: Gideon. Beat: resolution; inheritance transformed from sentence into responsibility.
